summary: tpu-inference's ragged paged attention v3 Pallas kernel (kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py), the default RPA: ragged_paged_attention(queries, keys, values, kv_cache, kv_lens, page_indices, cu_q_lens, distribution) over a paged KV cache shaped [total_num_pages, page_size, num_kv_heads_x2 // kv_packing, kv_packing, head_dim], K and V interleaved per head and packed by dtype (get_kv_cache_shape); decode, prefill and mixed cases each tuned by (bq_sz, bkv_sz, bq_csz, bkv_csz) block sizes, plus vmem_limit_bytes, chunk_prefill_size, sliding_window, soft_cap and q/k/v scales. Its shape checks: page_size must be a multiple of the KV dtype packing (kv_packing = 32 // bits: 2 for bf16, 4 for fp8/int8); bkv_sz and bkv_csz must be whole pages (multiples of page_size), with bkv_sz % bkv_csz == 0 and bq_sz % bq_csz == 0; head_dim % 128 == 0.
note: Was the kernels directory (tree/main/tpu_inference/kernels): a tree page summarised slowly enough to time out at 600 s twice in the gemma-4-31B-it hill-climb on v6e-8, losing the lookup each time. Now the one file most questions about it reach. The id is kept because pages and evals name it. The other kernels (flash_attention, mla, fused_moe, megablox, quantized_matmul, collectives, sparse_core) are siblings of ragged_paged_attention/ under tpu_inference/kernels/; batched_rpa has its own row (tpu-inference-batched-rpa), and which of the two a server runs is tpu-inference-attention-dispatch.

summary: Data parallelism as independent vllm serve processes on one TPU host behind a round-robin proxy (rr_proxy.py): each rank is pinned to its own chips with TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS=<chip list>, TPU_CHIPS_PER_PROCESS_BOUNDS=1,<chips per rank>,1 and TPU_PROCESS_BOUNDS=1,1,1, on its own port, with --data-parallel-* flags stripped; chips per rank is ceil(TP / cores per chip), CORES_PER_CHIP defaulting to 2 for v7x; cleanup kills the servers, frees /dev/vfio and /dev/accel, and removes /tmp/libtpu_lockfile. Written because vLLM's internal DP balancer refreshes rank load only every 100 ms and skews under bursty load.
note: The libtpu environment that lets several processes share one host, which nothing else in the catalog shows. Launching two TP 4 processes on a v6e-8 without it crashed libtpu (SLICE_FAILURE_CHIP_DRIVER_ERROR, net_util.cc RET_CHECK client_devices.size() >= num_addressable_devices) in the gemma-4-31B-it hill-climb, which then served TP 4 x DP 2 from one process. The script is tpu-inference's (JAX); the variables are libtpu's, but this recipe has not been run under torch_tpu or on v6e. The script only sets CORES_PER_CHIP for v7x (2); v6e has one TensorCore per chip (cloud-tpu-v6e, hw-tpu-v6e), so CORES_PER_CHIP=1 there is inferred, not the script's, and whether 1,4,1 bounds suit a v6e-8's 2x4 chips is not established here.

summary: How tpu-model-onboarding chooses --tensor-parallel-size and --data-parallel-size for vLLM on torch_tpu (tp_plan.json from engine_compatibility_check.py): a TP the user states wins, then a patch-registry model's validated serving settings; otherwise the largest TP that divides the devices, suits the query, KV and linear-attention head counts, has a torch_tpu device layout, is accepted by vLLM and whose weight shard fits 80% of one device's HBM, with DP = devices / TP.
